## Detailed entries

### Allen Park

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-09 (City Council adopted an emergency ordinance)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-09` (exact)
- **Duration:** 6 months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `mi-allen-park-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Emergency ordinance imposing a six-month moratorium on data centers (number not located)
- **What prompted it:** Solstice Data's proposed 26 MW data center at 7500 Enterprise Drive (site plan denied by the Planning Commission on 2026-06-04); noise, diesel generator emissions, water and power concerns
- **Affected projects:** Solstice Data 26 MW edge data center, 7500 Enterprise Drive (preliminary site plan denied 2026-06-04)
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; the six-month emergency moratorium adopted 2026-06-09 runs to about early December 2026.
- **Outcome:** Council also tightened the noise-control ordinance

### Brandon Township

- **Type:** Township
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-05-04 (Resolution #424-26, 6-0 roll call; Blair absent); extended 180 days by unanimous board vote at the regular meeting on the Monday before 2026-09-19 (about 2026-09-14)

### Caledonia Township

- **Type:** Township
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-02-04 (Board of Trustees approved the Resolution enacting a temporary moratorium on applications for Zoning and Building Review with respect to Data Centers and Digital Mining Uses by unanimous voice vote; applies retroactively to applications received since 2026-01-01)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-02-04` (exact)
- **Duration:** Initially about four months (to 2026-06-17 per the township manager's memo; the Board struck the 'lasting until Wednesday, June 17, 2026' wording at adoption); extended on 2026-06-03 until 2026-10-17. A further extension (Board resolution on the 2026-09-16 agenda; zoning-ordinance moratorium to 2027-02-17 heard by the Planning Commission on 2026-09-21) is pending.
- **Current end date:** `2026-10-17`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `mi-caledonia-township-undated`
- **Legal basis:** Board of Trustees resolution enacting a temporary moratorium on applications for Zoning and Building Review with respect to Data Centers and Digital Mining Uses (2026-02-04); extension resolution of 2026-06-03 (to 2026-10-17). No resolution numbers appear in the minutes or agendas. A proposed zoning amendment adding Section 23.11 (moratorium to 2027-02-17) was set for Planning Commission public hearing on 2026-09-21.
- **What prompted it:** Proactive pause on zoning and building review for data centers and digital mining operations; specific trigger not stated in the record reviewed
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Detailed status:** Extended; active as of 2026-09-23, running through 2026-10-17 under the June 3, 2026 extension. A further 'Resolution Extending The Temporary Moratorium' was on the Board's 2026-09-16 agenda (outcome not yet published) and the Planning Commission held a 2026-09-21 hearing on a zoning-ordinance moratorium lasting until 2027-02-17; a permanent Data Centers and Digital Mining zoning ordinance (Section 3.61) is in draft.
- **Outcome:** Board unanimously extended the moratorium through 2026-10-17; a second extension (to 2027-02-17 via zoning ordinance, and a Board resolution) was in process in September 2026 while a permanent data center and digital mining ordinance is drafted

### Cascade Charter Township (Kent County)

- **Type:** Township
- **Status:** ⚪ Expired

- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-11` (exact)
- **Duration:** Six months following the effective date (publication, 2026-03-17) or until data center zoning amendments take effect, whichever occurs first; extendable by resolution for up to six more months

- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `mi-cascade-charter-township-kent-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 002 of 2026, 'An Ordinance to Impose a Moratorium on the Issuance of Permits, Licenses or Approvals for Data Centers' (adopted by Resolution 010-2026, 2026-03-11; effective on publication 2026-03-17)
- **What prompted it:** Zoning ordinance lacks data center regulations; Microsoft data center proposals in nearby Lowell and Gaines townships; resident concerns about water (PFAS), energy, and noise

- **Affected projects:** A data-center waiver request was rejected in July 2026 (per MLive headline)
- **Detailed status:** Replaced 2026-09-06; Ordinance No. 2026-01 (adopted 2026-08-25) makes data centers a special land use in the M-1/M-2 districts with specific standards, and Resolution 2026-47 ended the moratorium when that ordinance took effect.
- **Outcome:** Replaced by Ordinance No. 2026-01: data centers are a special land use in the M-1 and M-2 districts, with residential setbacks, noise studies, utility capacity checks and decommissioning plans

### Zeeland Charter Township

- **Type:** Township
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-09-01 (unanimous Township Board vote on a resolution enacting temporary moratoria on energy facilities and data centers; it repealed and replaced the township's earlier data-center-only moratorium, Resolution No. 1027, adopted 2026-03-03)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-09-01` (exact)
- **Duration:** Initial term of 365 days following the effective date (effective on publication of the notice of adoption); counsel said it may then be extended in 60-day increments until the master plan update is complete
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, solar, wind, battery storage, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `mi-zeeland-charter-township-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Township Board resolution 'A Resolution Enacting Temporary Moratoria on Energy Facilities and Data Centers' adopted 2026-09-01 under Section 3.36 of the Zeeland Charter Township Zoning Ordinance (number blank in the board packet); it repealed and superseded the township's March 3, 2026 moratorium (No. 1027), which has its own row
- **What prompted it:** Master plan update underway; Silver Maple Solar (RWE Americas, ~200 MW) dispute and township lawsuit challenging PA 233; desire to maintain status quo on energy facilities and data centers until zoning is updated
- **Affected projects:** Silver Maple Solar (RWE Americas, ~1,900 acres in Zeeland and Jamestown townships); no data center application pending
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; one-year moratorium on commercial energy facilities (solar, wind, battery storage) and data centers (definition includes crypto-mining facilities) adopted 2026-09-01, runs 365 days from publication of the notice of adoption (approximately early September 2027).
- **Outcome:** Planning Commission and staff to complete master plan update and renewable-energy/data-center zoning before the moratorium ends

- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-03` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months
- **Current end date:** `—`

- **What prompted it:** Rising data center interest in West Michigan; zoning ordinance did not contemplate data centers (water, electricity, noise, light, vibration); Planning Commission busy with renewable-energy ordinance for Silver Maple Solar and a master plan update.
